blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Account deletion keeps every personal field of the member) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
_conn.execute(
    "UPDATE users SET deleted_at = datetime('now'), password_hash = NULL WHERE id = ?",
    (user_id,),
)
findings.recommendation: Erase the personal data on deletion, as the proposal promises: delete the users row, or overwrite email, display_name, phone and postal_address (email needs a unique non-identifying placeholder because of its UNIQUE NOT NULL constraint) so that the orders kept for accounting point to a row with no personal data. GDPR Art. 17 (erasure) and Art. 5(1)(e) (storage limitation).
findings.title: Account deletion keeps every personal field of the member

findings.recommendation: Add a test asserting that after delete_account no row of users still holds the member's email, display name, phone or postal address, while their orders remain.
findings.title: Tests do not check that personal data is erased

findings.recommendation: State what happens to analytics events on deletion: delete them at the analytics processor by analytics_id, or make the id unlinkable (per-user random id deleted with the account). Identify the analytics processor (GDPR Art. 28) if it is a third party.
findings.title: Erasure does not reach analytics data linked by analytics_id

findings.evidence: - A "Delete my account" button erases the member's personal data and signs them out everywhere; their orders are kept for accounting, without personal data.
findings.recommendation: State the retention of the soft-deleted row (if any is kept) and of the orders, and how erasure reaches backups of members.db (expiry window or re-applying deletions on restore). GDPR Art. 5(1)(e).
findings.title: Retention of deleted accounts and backups is not defined
